**Finding: Compliant** (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on us:

- **No MFN language exists.** Targeted searches for "most favoured/favored nation," "no less favorable," "favorable," best-terms, and matching/extension language all returned zero hits.
- **Pricing is fixed, not benchmarked.** The tiered per-trade schedule (p0059–p0067), Supplemental Payments (p0078), rebate shares (p0076), and support fees (p0086–p0089) are all fixed commercial terms. Nothing requires us to extend Licensor terms we grant to third parties or to match a third-party offer.
- **The only parity language runs in our favour.** Article VII(g) (p0094) obliges *Licensor* to make Revisions available to us when it releases them generally to its other licensees — a benefit to Customer, which the rule's detection guidance expressly directs not to flag.
- **The Right of First Refusal is a different animal.** Article XXII (p0139–p0141) requires us to notify Licensor of a bona fide third-party offer to buy our assets or merge, and gives Licensor five business days to exercise. Although this is a burden on us with a matching flavour, it is a change-of-control ROFR, not a pricing/best-terms MFN. I left it to the ROFR/change-of-control rule rather than double-flagging the same commercial term — worth confirming that rule is in scope for this review, since the five-business-day exercise window and the absence of any carve-out for financing or internal reorganisations are the substantive concerns there.
